title: Uniform regularity of kernels of coherent free-sheaf quotients
statement:
Fix integers $n\geq0$, $r\geq1$, and a polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$. There is an integer $a$, depending only on $n,r,P$, such that the following holds for every field $k$ [def-weil-field]. On $\mathbf P^n_k$ let
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal K\longrightarrow\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow0$$
be a short exact sequence of coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose that $\chi(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(d))=P(d)$ for every integer $d$, where $\chi$ is the alternating sum of finite coherent-cohomology dimensions [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Then $\mathcal K$ is $a$-regular, meaning
$$H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal K(a-j))=0\quad(1\leq j\leq n).$$
Here $\mathcal G(d)=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O(d)$, with twists as in [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and $H^j$ is module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, statement and proof; regularity is Tag 08A3, definition-regularity.

proof.text: Prove the assertion by induction on $n$, simultaneously for every $r\geq1$, every rational polynomial $P$, and every field. For $n=0$ the defining range $1\leq j\leq n$ is empty, so take $a=0$. For $n>0$ set $\Delta P(t)=P(t)-P(t-1)$ and choose the integer $m'$ supplied by the induction hypothesis for $(n-1,r,\Delta P)$. Put $b=\max(1,m')$. These choices precede any choice of field or quotient.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.

proof.text: Use the field-extension lemma with $L=k(u)$, which is infinite since the powers of the indeterminate $u$ are distinct. It preserves the coherent free quotient and every value $P(d)$, and reflects $a$-regularity for every integer $a$. Thus it suffices to construct the same bound over infinite fields.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.

proof.text: Over the infinite field choose the common regular hyperplane for $\mathcal F,\mathcal K,\mathcal O^{\oplus r},\mathcal O_X$. The restricted-quotient lemma gives the coherent exact quotient $0\to K_H\to\mathcal O_H^{\oplus r}\to F_H\to0$ and $\chi(H,F_H(d))=\Delta P(d)$. Since $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$, induction makes $K_H$ $m'$-regular. The regularity consequences make it $b$-regular. The common hyperplane also gives injective multiplication on $\mathcal K$ at every twist.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology-tail lemma to $E=\mathcal K$ at $m=b$. With $h_b=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal K(b))$, its two clauses give $H^j(X,\mathcal K(t))=0$ for $j\geq2,t\geq b$, and $H^1(X,\mathcal K(t))=0$ for $t\geq b+h_b$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.

proof.text: Apply the numerical first-cohomology estimate at $b\geq1$, using the higher vanishing just obtained. It gives $0\leq h_b\leq P(b)$. Define $N=\max(0,\lceil P(b)\rceil)$; then $h_b\leq N$ and $N$ depends only on $n,r,P$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.

proof.text: Choose $a=b+N+n+1$. Then $a-1\geq b+N\geq b+h_b$, so step 4 gives $H^1(X,\mathcal K(a-1))=0$. For $2\leq j\leq n$ one has $a-j\geq b$, so step 4 gives $H^j(X,\mathcal K(a-j))=0$. This is $a$-regularity. Every number depends only on $n,r,P$, and step 2 descends the same bound to the original field. If no quotient with polynomial $P$ exists the assertion is vacuous; the formula still defines an integer.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, assembly of the extracted arguments with the corrected enlarged regularity bound.
